name: Slendertone

card.summary: An Irish electrical muscle stimulation brand best known for abdominal toning belts that contract the core muscles to help build a firmer-looking midsection.
card.note: Marketed for toning; regulators have objected to weight- or girth-loss claims for such belts.

quick.overview:
Slendertone makes wearable electrical muscle stimulation (EMS) devices, the best known being a belt with gel pads that sends pulses through the abdominal muscles to make them contract. Users wear it for toning sessions as a way to work the core without doing crunches.

The brand began in Ireland and was revived in 2023 after its original company went into liquidation. Studies of powered muscle stimulators exist, but they mostly concern the device category; the FDA treats over-the-counter units as toning devices only.
quick.how: The belt is worn around the waist with gel pads against the skin and run for sessions of around half an hour a few days a week, with intensity adjusted by the user. Pads wear out and are replaced. Many people use it alongside regular training and diet.
quick.risks: Skin irritation and burns are possible side effects of EMS in general, and pacemaker users and people with certain conditions are advised to avoid it. The FDA and FTC have acted against ab belts that claimed weight or inch loss; a review of FDA records found a small number of reported adverse events.

lead: Slendertone is a consumer brand of electrical muscle stimulation (EMS) devices, best known for abdominal toning belts that use electrical pulses through gel pads to make the abdominal muscles contract. People use them to tone and firm the midsection as part of an effort to look leaner and more defined.[1]
According to Grokipedia, the brand originated in Ireland with Bio-Medical Research Ltd, which entered liquidation in June 2022, after which the brand was acquired in 2023 by a new Irish company.[1]
Research on the category includes an FDA 510(k) review of powered muscle stimulators cleared between 2000 and 2018.[2] EMS in general has a history in sport science and rehabilitation.[3]

chain: Belt pads deliver electrical pulses to abdominal muscles
Increased muscle tone over repeated sessions
angle.text: The belt is used to contract the abdominal muscles, aiming for a firmer midsection. Users typically pair it with training and nutrition, since EMS itself burns few calories.

infobox: Bio-Medical Research Ltd; revived 2023 as Bio-Medical Science and Technology Ltd[1]
OTC EMS devices may be marketed for muscle toning only[3]

paras: The flagship belt uses a three-pad arrangement intended to stimulate the upper and lower rectus abdominis, transverse abdominis and obliques, with sessions lasting around 30 minutes and adjustable intensity.[1] Gel pads need periodic replacement.[1]

Grokipedia describes Slendertone as arising from 1960s Irish work adapting clinical EMS for consumer toning, with growth through the 1990s, a 2016 connected belt shown at CES, and a claim of over seven million abdominal belts sold since 2000.[1] The original company entered liquidation in June 2022 and the brand was bought and relaunched in 2023.[1]
Separately, EMS itself traces to Galvani's 1761 work, and Soviet sport scientists used it with elite athletes in the 1960s.[3]

The FDA classifies EMS devices as over-the-counter (toning only) or prescription, and an import alert treats devices claiming girth reduction or weight loss as misbranded. The FTC charged three top-selling electronic ab belts with false claims in 2002.[3]

Contraindications include pacemakers and certain medical conditions; skin irritation and burns can occur.[3] A review of FDA records found 36 adverse event reports in a decade for powered muscle stimulators.[2]

No peer-reviewed trial of Slendertone specifically is included here. A 2020 cross-sectional analysis of 117 FDA 510(k)-cleared powered muscle stimulators from 2000 to 2018 described how marketing shifted from toning toward pain and circulation, and noted consumer popularity.[2] Wikipedia notes that EMS research results depend on protocol and that calorie burn is marginal.[3]
